tossups.text: A guild of wax merchants that functioned as this historical state's commercial court was called the "Saint John's Hundred." This state was likely partly governed by a group of magistrates and nobles that assembled in the "Chamber of Facets." In this state, a drawing of a four-legged animal with the caption "I am a wild beast" was produced by a six-year-old boy, whose doodles are among this state's thousand-plus excavated birch-bark documents. This state, which was home to the young artist Onfim, contained a kontor of the Hanseatic League called the Peterhof. Inhabitants of this state chose mayors called posadniki in a popular assembly that any citizen could theoretically convene by ringing a bell. This state's veche ("v'YETCH-yeh") was dissolved in 1478, when Ivan III brought its lands under Muscovy's rule. For 10 points, name this medieval merchant republic in northern Rus' ("ROOSE") that was centered on a city called "Veliky."

Description acceptable. A 1983 thesis on algorithms for this task notes the inadequacy of rule-based or table-based schemes, and invents a better approach to this task using a packed trie ("try") data structure. The paper that introduced Bloom filters gives this task as a sample application. A popular algorithm for this task was made by Frank Liang, who wrote the "patgen" program to generate the patterns it uses. In one system, parameters like "tolerance" and "pretolerance" affect whether this action is allowed, and performing this action results in a penalty, where a penalty of 10,000 means this action is disabled. The "overfull hbox" error directly results from LaTeX ("LAY-tech") failing to perform this task, meaning the user might need to manually specify it for certain words. For 10 points, name this typesetting task often paired with justification to ensure that text is spaced well, which is especially important when columns are narrow.
acceptableAnswers: accept descriptions of adding line breaks to text

tossups.text: Based on the account of a merchant named Diogenes, several places along the coast of this body of water have been proposed as the site of an important port trading in tortoise shells called Rhapta. Roman sources described towns on this body of water south of Opone like Nikon and Serapion in Azania. According to one theory, the Ma'anyan people were brought west across this body of water as laborers and slaves, settling one island around 500 to 700 AD. Cities like Muziris on this body of water, the largest described in the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, were at the eastern end of the sea-based Incense Road. Austronesians originating in Borneo settled an island in this body of water, mixing with the native African population. For 10 points, name this body of water whose monsoons were used by ancient sailors from the Chola Empire and crossed by the settlers of Madagascar.

This author wrote about the Paliau cargo cult on Manus in New Lives for Old and transcribed tape-recorded discussions with James Baldwin to create A Rap on Race. This anthropologist compared gender roles in different cultures in Male and Female and Sex and Temperament in Three Primitive Societies, while she studied family and education on Manus in Growing Up in New Guinea. Her most famous work discussed the taupou system of ceremonial virginity and was challenged by Derek Freeman. The author of an early book of popular anthropology contrasting Pacific Island and American girls' adolescences, for 10 points, name this American anthropologist who wrote Coming of Age in Samoa.

An equation modeling the movement of this substance can be simplified by the Dupuit-Forchheimer ("doo-PWEE FORK-high-mer") assumption. Graphs showing the movement of this substance feature a "rising limb." The Theis ("tice") equation describes the movement of this substance, and is more widely-used than another equation derived from applying a mass balance to Darcy's law. The phreatic ("free-ATTIC") zone lies below a "table" named for this substance, which lowers into a cone of depression in a process that depletes this resource called overdrafting. Many fields are circular as a result of using a "center-pivot" method of delivering this substance, which is also used to cool off livestock. The Dust Bowl resulted from the lack of this resource, which is distributed to crops via irrigation. For 10 points, name this substance found in aquifers.

Richard Taylor tried to assist troops stationed here with an ultimately unsuccessful counter-attack against a regiment of black soldiers at Milliken's Bend, while John Hunt Morgan almost crossed into Pennsylvania in an attempt to draw opposing forces from this city. Engagements in a campaign named for this city included the Battles of Champion's Hill and Port Gibson, the latter of which resulted in troops under William T. Sherman turning the city of Jackson into a "chimneyville". Shortly after this city fell, another Union victory in the same theatre was secured in the Battle of Port Hudson. Confederates in this city finally surrendered on July 4th, 1863. For 10 points, name this site of a prolonged siege by Ulysses S. Grant to give the Union control of the Mississippi River.

This composer used a wordless female choir in the "Sirens" movement of an orchestral work inspired by the paintings of Whistler. In the printed score for another set of his works, the titles appear at the end of each piece rather than at the beginning. Those are his preludes for piano, which include pieces like "What the West Wind Saw," "The Sunken Cathedral," and "The Girl With the Flaxen Hair," and he wrote three Nocturnes for orchestra. His best-known piano piece takes its title from a poem by Paul Verlaine and is the third movement of his Suite bergamasque. For 10 points, name this French impressionist composer who wrote La mer, Prelude to the Afternoon of a Faun, and Clair de lune.

One character in this novel has his name crossed out of the family bible after he marries a woman behind his father's back. That female character is sent a small piano sold at an estate auction. The protagonist of this novel entertains Lord Steyne at a charade party by performing Clytemnestra, after which her husband Rawdon Crawley is arrested. The protagonist of this novel throws a dictionary out of a carriage after graduating from Miss Pinkerton's Academy with Amelia Sedley, who marries George Osborne. For 10 points, name this novel about Becky Sharp, written by William Thackeray.

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for sweat glands. It plays a key role in the integumentary system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this hair follicle-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The hair follicle is a key component of the Integumentary system, involved in sweat glands.

tossups.text: Eight atoms of this element in a rhomboid cluster form this element's "red" allotrope. A carboxylic acid contains one atom of this element double-bonded to carbon. After fluorine, this is the second most electronegative element. An allotrope of this element absorbs ultraviolet light in the atmosphere. That allotrope, ozone, is made up of three atoms of this element. For 10 points, identify this element with atomic number 8 and atomic symbol O.

A study by PM Markey using the fake names Jake and Suzy Harmen found that these peoples' behavior in real life extended to the internet. These people's behavior were studied by John Darely and Bibb Latane. In one experiment, a person filling out a questionnaire ignored smoke filling the room when these people were present. Diffusion of responsibility is one explanation for these people's behavior, while Good Samaritan Laws exist to encourage these people to take action. These people were falsely claimed to have allowed the murder of Kitty Genovese. For 10 points, name these people who may ignore someone in need according to their namesake effect.
acceptableAnswers: accept answers referring to things like other people

tossups.text: Foreigners living in this polity without citizenship rights were known as "metics." This polity's government was reworked into an oligarchy known as the Thirty Tyrants following this polity's loss in one war. The lawgiver Cleisthenes [KLYSE-thuh-neez] established this polity's practice of a vote to banish, known as ostracism. The orator Pericles gave a famous funeral oration during this polity's "Golden Age." For ten points, name this Greek city-state defeated by Sparta in the Peloponnesian War.

The volley principle and phase locking are phenomena involved in this perception. Two opposing theories of this sense focus on location and frequency of neuronal response, respectively; the latter is the place code. The round and oval windows are involved in transmitting and transducing its stimuli. This sense uses the precedence effect and detects time differences to conduct scene analysis and localization. This sense is primarily processed in the temporal lobe, and stimuli of this sense is transduced by the organ of Corti, amplified by the ossicles, and transmitted by the tympanic membrane's vibrations. For 10 points, name this sense that perceives sound using the ears.

This procedure is done on air-sensitive material using a Perkin triangle. The number of stages involved in one kind of this procedure can be derived from a VLE plot using the McCabe-Thiele method, which is used in designing binary columns. Most versions of this procedure do not work on azeotropes. The Fenske equation can be used to calculate the number of theoretical plates in its fractional variety. For 10 points, name this procedure that separates components of a liquid mixture using differences in their boiling points.

this structure is essential for parathyroid hormone. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this thyroid-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The thyroid is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in parathyroid hormone.

tossups.text: A poem from this country asks "O fellow citizen, / What have they done to us?" to an object with "hard bitumen around [its] feet." The speaker of a poem from this country receives a letter "written with a thumb-nail dipped in tar" that states "we don't know where he are." The Jindyworobak ("JIN-dee-WOH-roh-back") movement was based in this home country of an author who adopted a name meaning "paperbark tree," Oodgeroo Noonuccal ("OO-juh-roo noo-NUCK-ul"). A poet from this country, who wrote "Clancy of the Overflow," feuded with Henry Lawson in the "Bulletin Debate." A song about a "jolly swagman" who camped "under the shade of a coolibah tree" is one of this country's "bush ballads." For 10 points, name this home country of Banjo Paterson, who wrote the poem "Waltzing Matilda."

The normalization constant for a partition function in n-dimensional phase space is this quantity to the negative n. Precise measurements of this constant in 2017 will enable the kilogram SI unit to be physically defined for the first time. The first energy level of a particle-in-a-box is this quantity squared over eight mL-squared. The Compton wavelength is defined as this quantity over mass times the speed of light. This quantity was plugged into the numerator of an exponential to prevent the Rayleigh-Jeans law from diverging at high frequencies. A photon's energy equals its frequency times this constant. The reduced form of this constant gets a bar written across it. For 10 points, identify this value named for the formulator of quantum theory, which is symbolized h.

This treaty was signed at the home of George Hays while one force waited nearby at Parkzicht. In the discussion leading up to it, delegates expressed fear that a backlash over a recent skirmish at Holkrans would derail peace efforts, but realization that their situation had worsened since the failed Hatherley proposal led to the eventual rejection of the plan of Marthinus Steyn. It was precipitated by an offer of mediation by Abraham Kuyper, which led to the Klerksdorp Conference and to the formal surrender at Melrose House. Drawn up by James Hertzog and Jan Smuts, For 10 points, name this document that deferred voting rights for people of color, guaranteed right of return for Uitlanders and Dutch language schools in the Orange Free State and Transvaal, and ended the Boer War.

Deirdre McCloskey critiqued the tendency of people in this profession to equate statistical significance with scientific significance. A scholar in this profession studied the Mariel Boatlift using difference-in-differences analysis. This profession's use of targets and instruments was pioneered by Jan Tinbergen ("yahn TIN-bairg-in"). Its practitioners often get their data from a nonprofit named for it, the NBER. Empirical rules developed by this profession include Okun's law, which can be explained by a multiplier effect. Techniques like variable autoregression are used in a discipline whose name is a portmanteau of this profession and "metrics." Paul Samuelson wrote a popular textbook for studying, for 10 points, what profession of Paul Krugman?

This man won election to office when his nation's congress chose him over the former president Jorge Alessandri, and shortly afterwards the head of his country's military, Rene Schneider, was kidnapped by terrorists. One of this man's most notable actions in office was the nationalization of his country's copper industry, at the time its leading export and he saw a prolonged strike by truck owners hamper his attempts to govern. Carlos Prats put down the Tanquetazo coup attempt against this man in 1973, but later that year this man was found dead from a gunshot wound during the coup that replaced him. For 10 points name this Socialist president of Chile from 1970-1973 who preceded Augusto Pinochet.

Strains of Wolbachia have been engineered to prevent the reproduction these insects, which are the vectors for dengue fever and malaria.

Variable stars change brightness due to the kappa-mechanism, changes between this element's singly and doubly ionized forms, which have different opacity, at their outer portion.
Regions of the doubly ionized form of this element tend to be giant molecular clouds and hotspots of star formation. This element is the lightest and most abundant one in the universe.
